articles.title: Fauci Perjury Files: Rand Paul Demands DOJ Prosecute America's Doctor for Lying to Congress on Gain-of-Function
articles.summary: Senator Rand Paul has formally referred Dr. Anthony Fauci to the Department of Justice for criminal perjury, alleging Fauci knowingly lied under oath in 2021 when he denied NIH funding of gain-of-function research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. Internal documents and grant records obtained through congressional investigation directly contradict Fauci's sworn testimony. If prosecuted, this would mark the most significant accountability action against a federal health official in modern history.

articles.title: Fauci's Secret Diary Exposed: Praised Beijing, Trashed Trump, Lost Classified Files in Ransomware Attack

articles.title: Antidepressants: The Harm Data Big Psychiatry Doesn't Want You to Read
articles.summary: A scientific review published in Spektrum examines the growing body of evidence on the benefits and harms of antidepressants — drugs now prescribed to hundreds of millions worldwide despite unresolved mechanistic questions and documented risks including emotional blunting, sexual dysfunction, and dependency. The review arrives as prescribing rates continue to climb globally, with regulatory agencies consistently downplaying harm signals in favor of industry-friendly efficacy narratives. Critics argue the informed consent process for these drugs remains fundamentally broken.

articles.title: Off-Patent Cancer Drugs Like Ivermectin Are Being Buried — Dr. Makis Names the Profit Motive
articles.summary: Canadian oncologist Dr. William Makis is making the case that cheap, off-patent repurposed drugs — including ivermectin — show genuine mechanistic and clinical promise against multiple cancer types, yet are systematically ignored because they cannot be patented and monetized. The profit architecture of oncology actively suppresses investigation of these compounds, leaving terminal patients without options that exist in the published literature. Makis argues the medical establishment's silence on repurposed drugs is not scientific — it is financial.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Device Safety Failures From Investors — SEC Fraud Lawsuit Exposes FDA Compliance Lies
articles.summary: A securities fraud class action has been filed against Beta Bionics after its stock collapsed over 37% following disclosure that the company allegedly misrepresented the safety, efficacy, and FDA compliance status of its iLet automated insulin delivery device. Investors claim executives knew about critical safety issues and concealed them while continuing to promote the product. The case raises broader questions about how medical device makers exploit FDA approval optics to mislead both patients and markets.

articles.title: COVID Fraud: Plano Clinics to Pay $20M After Billing Nasal Swabs as Full Office Visits — Who Was Watching?
articles.summary: A network of COVID testing clinics in Plano, Texas has agreed to pay $20 million to settle federal allegations that they systematically billed simple nasal swab tests as full office visits, defrauding federal uninsured patient programs during the pandemic. The scheme exploited the regulatory chaos and emergency funding flows of COVID-era healthcare with apparent impunity for years before being caught. The settlement exposes the systemic fraud that flourished under emergency public health infrastructure with minimal oversight.

His death follows a pattern critics have long identified: whistleblowers who expose powerful connections to Epstein face devastating personal consequences.

articles.title: Mebendazole Beats Gefitinib Resistance in Lung Cancer — Will Oncology Ignore Another Off-Patent Answer?
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed PLOS ONE study demonstrates that mebendazole, a decades-old antiparasitic drug costing pennies per dose, synergizes with EGFR-targeted therapy to overcome drug resistance in non-small cell lung cancer — one of oncology's most intractable treatment failures. The research reveals a dual mechanism targeting both EGFR signaling and microtubule dynamics, suppressing tumor growth where billion-dollar targeted therapies have failed. With no patent potential, this compound faces the same institutional indifference that has buried other repurposed drug candidates.
